title: The Sealed Envelope
briefing: payments-api was deployed this morning and has not started once. The database password was supposed to arrive in an envelope: a Secret named db-credentials, which nobody ever made. The DBA left the password on a sticky note (case/sticky-note.txt). Seal it properly, and make sure the service really gets in: a password that is almost right is as good as none.
objective: Put the database password in a Secret and bring payments-api up, connected to the database.
hints: Ask the pod what it is waiting for: `kubectl describe` shows why its container cannot be created.
The Deployment reads the password from the key `password` of a Secret called db-credentials. The sticky note has the value.
If the service starts but cannot log in, compare the password byte for byte. A Secret stores base64, and base64 encodes every byte you give it, including the newline that `echo` adds.
`kubectl create secret generic db-credentials --from-literal=password=...` never adds a newline; neither do `echo -n ... | base64` or `stringData`.

assert.label: the payments-api pod is ready and has not been restarted since it got in
the password in the Secret is exactly the one on the note

constraints.label: payments-api was not deleted and recreated

findings.clue: The container cannot be created: it needs the Secret db-credentials, and it does not exist.
The DBA's note: the payments role's password is correct-horse.
You looked inside the Secret. What is stored there has to match the note exactly: every byte counts.
